sanskrit: jñātidāsī yato jātā kaikeyyās tu sahoṣitā prāsādaṃ candrasaṃkāśam āruroha yadṛcchayā
english: A servant-maid born of Kaikeyī's kinsmen, who had lived there alongside her, happened to climb the palace that shone like the moon.

sanskrit: siktarājapathāṃ kṛtsnāṃ prakīrṇakamalotpalām ayodhyāṃ mantharā tasmāt prāsādād anvavaikṣata
english: From that palace Mantharā gazed out over the whole of Ayodhyā — its royal roads sprinkled with water and strewn with lotus blossoms and blue water-lilies.

sanskrit: patākābhir varārhābhir dhvajaiś ca samalaṃkṛtām siktāṃ candanatoyaiś ca śiraḥsnātajanair vṛtām
english: The city was adorned with precious banners and pennants, sprinkled with sandalwood water, and thronged with people who had bathed and washed their hair.

sanskrit: avidūre sthitāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhātrīṃ papraccha mantharā uttamenābhisaṃyuktā harṣeṇārthaparā satī
english: Seeing a nurse standing nearby, Mantharā — filled with great curiosity and intent on learning the reason — questioned her.

sanskrit: rāmamātā dhanaṃ kiṃ nu janebhyaḥ saṃprayacchati atimātraṃ praharṣo 'yaṃ kiṃ janasya ca śaṃsa me kārayiṣyati kiṃ vāpi saṃprahṛṣṭo mahīpatiḥ
english: "Why is Rāma's mother distributing wealth to the people? Tell me what is the reason for this extraordinary rejoicing. And what is the king so delighted about that he is about to do?"

sanskrit: vidīryamāṇā harṣeṇa dhātrī paramayā mudā ācacakṣe 'tha kubjāyai bhūyasīṃ rāghave śriyam
english: Bursting with joy and with supreme delight, the nurse then disclosed to the hunchback all the great glory that was about to come upon Rāghava.

sanskrit: śvaḥ puṣyeṇa jitakrodhaṃ yauvarājyena rāghavam rājā daśaratho rāmam abhiṣecayitānagham
english: "Tomorrow, under the Puṣya constellation, King Daśaratha will consecrate the sinless Rāma, conqueror of anger, as crown prince."

sanskrit: dhātryās tu vacanaṃ śrutvā kubjā kṣipram amarṣitā kailāsa śikharākārāt prāsādād avarohata
english: Upon hearing the nurse's words, the hunchback was immediately seized with indignation and descended swiftly from the palace, which had the appearance of a Kailāsa peak.

sanskrit: sā dahyamānā kopena mantharā pāpadarśinī śayānām etya kaikeyīm idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Burning with rage, Mantharā, that one of evil vision, went to Kaikeyī as she lay resting and spoke these words to her.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha mūḍhe kiṃ śeṣe bhayaṃ tvām abhivartate upaplutamahaughena kim ātmānaṃ na budhyase
english: "Arise, fool! Why do you lie there? Fear is fast approaching you. Submerged in a great flood, do you not understand your own situation?"

sanskrit: aniṣṭe subhagākāre saubhāgyena vikatthase calaṃ hi tava saubhāgyaṃ nadyaḥ srota ivoṣṇage
english: "You boast of your good fortune though its form is ill-omened. Your prosperity is as fleeting as the current of a river in summer."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu kaikeyī ruṣṭayā paruṣaṃ vacaḥ kubjayā pāpadarśinyā viṣādam agamat param
english: Addressed thus with harsh words by the evil-sighted hunchback in her anger, Kaikeyī fell into the deepest distress.

sanskrit: kaikeyī tv abravīt kubjāṃ kaccit kṣemaṃ na manthare viṣaṇṇavadanāṃ hi tvāṃ lakṣaye bhṛśaduḥkhitām
english: Kaikeyī then said to the hunchback: "Is everything not well with you, Mantharā? I see your face is downcast and you seem deeply distressed."

sanskrit: mantharā tu vacaḥ śrutvā kaikeyyā madhurākṣaram uvāca krodhasaṃyuktā vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradā
english: Having heard Kaikeyī's sweet words, Mantharā — that one skilled in speech — replied with words filled with rage.

sanskrit: sā viṣaṇṇatarā bhūtvā kubjā tasyā hitaiṣiṇī viṣādayantī provāca bhedayantī ca rāghavam
english: Becoming ever more despondent, the hunchback — claiming to act in Kaikeyī's interest — spoke to grieve her and to drive a wedge against Rāghava.

sanskrit: akṣemaṃ sumahad devi pravṛttaṃ tvadvināśanam rāmaṃ daśaratho rājā yauvarājye 'bhiṣekṣyati
english: "A great misfortune has come about, O queen — your ruin is at hand. King Daśaratha will consecrate Rāma as crown prince."

sanskrit: sāsmy agādhe bhaye magnā duḥkhaśokasamanvitā dahyamānānaleneva tvaddhitārtham ihāgatā
english: "I am plunged into a bottomless fear, overcome with grief and sorrow, burning as if in fire — and yet I have come here for your sake."

sanskrit: tava duḥkhena kaikeyi mama duḥkhaṃ mahad bhavet tvadvṛddhau mama vṛddhiś ca bhaved atra na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Your grief becomes my great grief, Kaikeyī, and your prosperity becomes my prosperity — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: narādhipakule jātā mahiṣī tvaṃ mahīpateḥ ugratvaṃ rājadharmāṇāṃ kathaṃ devi na budhyase
english: "Born into a royal lineage, you are the chief queen of the king. How is it, O goddess, that you do not understand the harsh realities of royal duty?"

sanskrit: dharmavādī śaṭho bhartā ślakṣṇavādī ca dāruṇaḥ śuddhabhāve na jānīṣe tenaivam atisaṃdhitā
english: "Your husband, though he speaks of righteousness, is a deceiver; though he speaks gently, he is cruel. In your pure-hearted state you do not know this, and so he has outwitted you."

sanskrit: upasthitaṃ prayuñjānas tvayi sāntvam anarthakam arthenaivādya te bhartā kausalyāṃ yojayiṣyati
english: "Your husband deploys soothing words toward you as a mere pretense — when it comes to actual benefit, today he will endow Kausalyā."

sanskrit: apavāhya sa duṣṭātmā bharataṃ tava bandhuṣu kālyaṃ sthāpayitā rāmaṃ rājye nihatakaṇṭake
english: "That evil-souled king, having sent Bharata away among your kinsmen, will tomorrow establish Rāma in the kingdom with all obstacles removed."

sanskrit: śatruḥ patipravādena mātreva hitakāmyayā āśīviṣa ivāṅkena bāle paridhṛtas tvayā
english: "An enemy under the guise of a husband, who appears to wish you well as a mother would — like a venomous serpent clasped to one's bosom — that is who you have taken to heart, dear girl."

sanskrit: yathā hi kuryāt sarpo vā śatrur vā pratyupekṣitaḥ rājñā daśarathenādya saputrā tvaṃ tathā kṛtā
english: "Just as a serpent or an enemy left unheeded would act, King Daśaratha has treated you together with your son today."

sanskrit: pāpenānṛtasāntvena bāle nityaṃ sukhocite rāmaṃ sthāpayatā rājye sānubandhā hatā hy asi
english: "By the wicked man's false soothing words, O young one, ever accustomed to comfort — by his installing Rāma in the kingdom — you together with your kin are truly ruined."

sanskrit: sā prāptakālaṃ kaikeyi kṣipraṃ kuru hitaṃ tava trāyasva putram ātmānaṃ māṃ ca vismayadarśane
english: "Therefore, Kaikeyī, act at once while there is still time — do what is for your good. Save your son, save yourself, and save me too, O you of wondrous appearance."

sanskrit: mantharāyā vacaḥ śrutvā śayanāt sā śubhānanā ekam ābharaṇaṃ tasyai kubjāyai pradadau śubham
english: Having heard Mantharā's words, the lovely-faced Kaikeyī rose from her couch and gave a fine ornament to that hunchback.

sanskrit: dattvā tv ābharaṇaṃ tasyai kubjāyai pramadottamā kaikeyī mantharāṃ hṛṣṭā punar evābravīd idam
english: Having given the ornament to the hunchback, Kaikeyī, most excellent of women, joyfully said this again to Mantharā:

sanskrit: idaṃ tu manthare mahyam ākhyāsi paramaṃ priyam etan me priyam ākhyātuḥ kiṃ vā bhūyaḥ karomi te
english: "This that you have told me, Mantharā, is most pleasing to me. What more can I do for you who have brought me such welcome news?"

sanskrit: rāme vā bharate vāhaṃ viśeṣaṃ nopalakṣaye tasmāt tuṣṭāsmi yad rājā rāmaṃ rājye 'bhiṣekṣyati
english: "I see no difference between Rāma and Bharata. Therefore I am pleased that the king will consecrate Rāma in the kingdom."

sanskrit: na me paraṃ kiṃ cid itas tvayā punaḥ priyaṃ priyārhe suvacaṃ vaco varam tathā hy avocas tvam ataḥ priyottaraṃ varaṃ paraṃ te pradadāmi taṃ vṛṇu
english: "There is nothing you could tell me that would please me more, O worthy one, well-spoken and excellent. Since you have spoken words that are all the more dear, I offer you a choice boon — choose it."

sanskrit: mantharā tv abhyasūyyainām utsṛjyābharaṇaṃ ca tat uvācedaṃ tato vākyaṃ kopaduḥkhasamanvitā
english: But Mantharā, envying her, flung back that ornament and spoke these words then filled with anger and sorrow:

sanskrit: harṣaṃ kim idam asthāne kṛtavaty asi bāliśe śokasāgaramadhyastham ātmānaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: "Why are you rejoicing so foolishly at the wrong moment, childish woman? Do you not understand that you stand in the midst of an ocean of grief?"

sanskrit: subhagā khalu kausalyā yasyāḥ putro 'bhiṣekṣyate yauvarājyena mahatā śvaḥ puṣyeṇa dvijottamaiḥ
english: "How fortunate indeed is Kausalyā, whose son will be consecrated tomorrow under the Puṣya star with the great ceremony of crown prince by the foremost of brahmins."

sanskrit: prāptāṃ sumahatīṃ prītiṃ pratītāṃ tāṃ hatadviṣam upasthāsyasi kausalyāṃ dāsīva tvaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: "That Kausalyā, triumphant and her enemies destroyed, will have attained supreme delight — and you will wait upon her with hands folded like a servant girl."

sanskrit: hṛṣṭāḥ khalu bhaviṣyanti rāmasya paramāḥ striyaḥ aprahṛṣṭā bhaviṣyanti snuṣās te bharatakṣaye
english: "The chief wives of Rāma will indeed be joyful. But your daughters-in-law will be joyless at Bharata's ruin."

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītāṃ bruvantīṃ mantharāṃ tataḥ rāmasyaiva guṇān devī kaikeyī praśaśaṃsa ha
english: Seeing Mantharā speaking thus, filled with great grief, Queen Kaikeyī praised Rāma's virtues.

sanskrit: dharmajño gurubhir dāntaḥ kṛtajñaḥ satyavāk śuciḥ rāmo rājñaḥ suto jyeṣṭho yauvarājyam ato 'rhati
english: "Rāma knows dharma, is restrained by his elders, is grateful, truth-speaking, and pure. As the king's eldest son, he rightly deserves the position of crown prince."

sanskrit: bhrātṝn bhṛtyāṃś ca dīrghāyuḥ pitṛvat pālayiṣyati saṃtapyase kathaṃ kubje śrutvā rāmābhiṣecanam
english: "Long-lived, he will care for his brothers and servants as a father does. How can you grieve, hunchback, upon hearing of Rāma's consecration?"

sanskrit: bharataś cāpi rāmasya dhruvaṃ varṣaśatāt param pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyam avāpsyati nararṣabhaḥ
english: "Bharata too, that bull among men, will certainly obtain the ancestral kingdom — his father's and grandfather's — after a hundred years in succession to Rāma."

sanskrit: sā tvam abhyudaye prāpte vartamāne ca manthare bhaviṣyati ca kalyāṇe kimarthaṃ paritapyase kausalyāto 'tiriktaṃ ca sa tu śuśrūṣate hi mām
english: "When prosperity has arrived, and is present, and good fortune is yet to come, why do you grieve, Mantharā? And moreover, Rāma serves me more than he does Kausalyā."

sanskrit: kaikeyyā vacanaṃ śrutvā mantharā bhṛśaduḥkhitā dīrgham uṣṇaṃ viniḥśvasya kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Having heard Kaikeyī's words, Mantharā, deeply grieved, sighed a long, hot sigh and said this to Kaikeyī:

sanskrit: anarthadarśinī maurkhyān nātmānam avabudhyase śokavyasanavistīrṇe majjantī duḥkhasāgare
english: "Blind to your own ruin through foolishness, you do not perceive your own situation — you who are sinking into an ocean of grief, wide with sorrow and calamity."

sanskrit: bhavitā rāghavo rājā rāghavasya ca yaḥ sutaḥ rājavaṃśāt tu bharataḥ kaikeyi parihāsyate
english: "Rāghava will be king, and then whoever is Rāghava's son — but Bharata, Kaikeyī, will be excluded from the royal line."

sanskrit: na hi rājñaḥ sutāḥ sarve rājye tiṣṭhanti bhāmini sthāpyamāneṣu sarveṣu sumahān anayo bhavet
english: "Not all sons of a king remain in the kingdom, O passionate one — for if all were to be installed, the transgression would be very great."

sanskrit: tasmāj jyeṣṭhe hi kaikeyi rājyatantrāṇi pārthivāḥ sthāpayanty anavadyāṅgi guṇavatsv itareṣv api
english: "Therefore, Kaikeyī, kings establish the mechanisms of rule in the eldest son — O you of faultless limbs — even when the others too are possessed of virtues."

sanskrit: asāv atyantanirbhagnas tava putro bhaviṣyati anāthavat sukhebhyaś ca rājavaṃśāc ca vatsale
english: "Your son will be utterly destitute, like one without a protector, cut off from comforts and from the royal line, dear one."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tvadarthe saṃprāptā tvaṃ tu māṃ nāvabudhyase sapatnivṛddhau yā me tvaṃ pradeyaṃ dātum icchasi
english: "I have come for your sake, yet you do not understand me — you who wish to give me a gift meant to celebrate a co-wife's advancement."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ tu bharataṃ rāmaḥ prāpya rājyam akaṇṭakam deśāntaraṃ nāyayitā lokāntaram athāpi vā
english: "Once Rāma has obtained an uncontested kingdom, he will certainly send Bharata away to another land — or even to another world."

sanskrit: bāla eva hi mātulyaṃ bharato nāyitas tvayā saṃnikarṣāc ca sauhārdaṃ jāyate sthāvareṣv api
english: "Bharata was sent to his maternal uncle's house while still a child and was not brought back by you — for affection grows even in stationary beings through proximity."

sanskrit: goptā hi rāmaṃ saumitrir lakṣmaṇaṃ cāpi rāghavaḥ aśvinor iva saubhrātraṃ tayor lokeṣu viśrutam
english: "Saumitri Lakṣmaṇa is Rāma's protector, and Rāghava is Lakṣmaṇa's — their fraternal bond is renowned in the worlds, like that of the twin Aśvins."

sanskrit: tasmān na lakṣmaṇe rāmaḥ pāpaṃ kiṃ cit kariṣyati rāmas tu bharate pāpaṃ kuryād iti na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Therefore Rāma will do no harm to Lakṣmaṇa — but that Rāma will do harm to Bharata, of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tasmād rājagṛhād eva vanaṃ gacchatu te sutaḥ etad dhi rocate mahyaṃ bhṛśaṃ cāpi hitaṃ tava
english: "Therefore let your son depart to the forest directly from the king's house. This is what I strongly favor, and it is greatly for your benefit."

sanskrit: evaṃ te jñātipakṣasya śreyaś caiva bhaviṣyati yadi ced bharato dharmāt pitryaṃ rājyam avāpsyati
english: "Thus it will be well for your kinsmen's side too, if Bharata obtains by right the paternal kingdom."

sanskrit: sa te sukhocito bālo rāmasya sahajo ripuḥ samṛddhārthasya naṣṭārtho jīviṣyati kathaṃ vaśe
english: "Your boy, accustomed to comfort, is Rāma's natural enemy — deprived of wealth while the other is prosperous, how will he live in subjection?"

sanskrit: abhidrutam ivāraṇye siṃhena gajayūthapam pracchādyamānaṃ rāmeṇa bharataṃ trātum arhasi
english: "Like the lord of an elephant herd in a forest attacked by a lion, Bharata being overwhelmed by Rāma — you ought to save him."

sanskrit: darpān nirākṛtā pūrvaṃ tvayā saubhāgyavattayā rāmamātā sapatnī te kathaṃ vairaṃ na yātayet
english: "Rāma's mother, your co-wife, was formerly humiliated by you in your pride and good fortune — how would she not now take revenge?"

sanskrit: yadā hi rāmaḥ pṛthivīm avāpsyati dhruvaṃ pranaṣṭo bharato bhaviṣyati ato hi saṃcintaya rājyam ātmaje parasya cādyaiva vivāsakāraṇam
english: "When Rāma obtains the earth, Bharata will certainly be destroyed. Therefore think at once of securing the kingdom for your own son — and of a cause for banishing the other's."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu kaikeyī krodhena jvalitānanā dīrgham uṣṇaṃ viniḥśvasya mantharām idam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, Kaikeyī — her face blazing with anger — breathed a long, hot breath and said this to Mantharā:

sanskrit: adya rāmam itaḥ kṣipraṃ vanaṃ prasthāpayāmy aham yauvarājyena bharataṃ kṣipram evābhiṣecaye
english: "Today I will send Rāma away from here quickly to the forest, and will swiftly consecrate Bharata as crown prince."

sanskrit: idaṃ tv idānīṃ saṃpaśya kenopāyena manthare bharataḥ prāpnuyād rājyaṃ na tu rāmaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "Now look at this: by what means, Mantharā, will Bharata obtain the kingdom and Rāma in no way obtain it?"

sanskrit: evam uktā tayā devyā mantharā pāpadarśinī rāmārtham upahiṃsantī kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the queen, Mantharā, evil-visioned, eager to harm Rāma's cause, said this to Kaikeyī:

sanskrit: hantedānīṃ pravakṣyāmi kaikeyi śrūyatāṃ ca me yathā te bharato rājyaṃ putraḥ prāpsyati kevalam
english: "Very well — I shall tell you now, Kaikeyī; listen to me and hear how your son Bharata alone will obtain the kingdom."

sanskrit: śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ tasyā mantharāyās tu kaikayī kiṃ cid utthāya śayanāt svāstīrṇād idam abravīt
english: Having heard those words of Mantharā's, Kaikeyī rose somewhat from her well-spread couch and spoke thus:

sanskrit: kathaya tvaṃ mamopāyaṃ kenopāyena manthare bharataḥ prāpnuyād rājyaṃ na tu rāmaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "Tell me the means — by what means, Mantharā, will Bharata obtain the kingdom and Rāma in no way obtain it?"

sanskrit: evam uktā tayā devyā mantharā pāpadarśinī rāmārtham upahiṃsantī kubjā vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the queen, Mantharā, evil-visioned, eager to harm Rāma's cause, the hunchback spoke these words:

sanskrit: tava devāsure yuddhe saha rājarṣibhiḥ patiḥ agacchat tvām upādāya devarājasya sāhyakṛt
english: "In the war between the gods and asuras, your husband went, taking you with him along with royal sages, to render aid to the king of gods."

sanskrit: diśam āsthāya kaikeyi dakṣiṇāṃ daṇḍakān prati vaijayantam iti khyātaṃ puraṃ yatra timidhvajaḥ
english: "Heading toward the southern direction, toward the Daṇḍaka region, toward the city known as Vaijayanta, where dwelt Timidhvaja —"

sanskrit: sa śambara iti khyātaḥ śatamāyo mahāsuraḥ dadau śakrasya saṃgrāmaṃ devasaṃghair anirjitaḥ
english: "— that one known as Śambara, the great asura of a hundred illusions, who had not been defeated by the hosts of gods, gave battle to Śakra."

sanskrit: tasmin mahati saṃgrāme rājā daśarathas tadā apavāhya tvayā devi saṃgrāmān naṣṭacetanaḥ
english: "In that great battle, King Daśaratha, having lost his senses, was carried away from the fighting by you, O queen."

sanskrit: tatrāpi vikṣataḥ śastraiḥ patis te rakṣitas tvayā tuṣṭena tena dattau te dvau varau śubhadarśane
english: "There too, your husband was wounded by weapons and was protected by you. Delighted with you, he granted you two boons, O beautiful one."

sanskrit: sa tvayoktaḥ patir devi yadeccheyaṃ tadā varau gṛhṇīyām iti tat tena tathety uktaṃ mahātmanā anabhijñā hy ahaṃ devi tvayaiva kathitaṃ purā
english: "You said to your husband then, O queen: 'Whenever I wish, I shall receive those two boons' — and that great-souled one said 'So be it.' I am not unaware of this, for you yourself told me long ago."

sanskrit: tau varau yāca bhartāraṃ bharatasyābhiṣecanam pravrājanaṃ ca rāmasya tvaṃ varṣāṇi caturdaśa
english: "Ask those two boons of your husband: the consecration of Bharata, and the banishment of Rāma for fourteen years."

sanskrit: krodhāgāraṃ praviśyādya kruddhevāśvapatisute śeṣvānantarhitāyāṃ tvaṃ bhūmau malinavāsinī mā smainaṃ pratyudīkṣethā mā cainam abhibhāṣathāḥ
english: "Enter the chamber of wrath today as though enraged, O daughter of Aśvapati; lie on the ground without your bed, dressed in soiled garments. Do not look at him nor speak to him."

sanskrit: dayitā tvaṃ sadā bhartur atra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ tvatkṛte ca mahārājo viśed api hutāśanam
english: "You are always dear to your husband — of this I have no doubt. For your sake the great king would even enter fire."

sanskrit: na tvāṃ krodhayituṃ śakto na kruddhāṃ pratyudīkṣitum tava priyārthaṃ rājā hi prāṇān api parityajet
english: "He cannot bear to make you angry, nor to face you when you are angry. Indeed, the king would give up his very life for what pleases you."

sanskrit: na hy atikramituṃ śaktas tava vākyaṃ mahīpatiḥ mandasvabhāve budhyasva saubhāgyabalam ātmanaḥ
english: "The lord of the earth is not capable of transgressing your word. Know your own power of good fortune, you who are slow to understand your own nature."

sanskrit: maṇimuktāsuvarṇāni ratnāni vividhāni ca dadyād daśaratho rājā mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "King Daśaratha would give gems, pearls, gold, and various jewels — do not set your mind on those."

sanskrit: yau tau devāsure yuddhe varau daśaratho 'dadāt tau smāraya mahābhāge so 'rtho mā tvām atikramet
english: "Those two boons that Daśaratha granted in the war between the gods and asuras — remind him of them, O illustrious one. Do not let that matter pass you by."

sanskrit: yadā tu te varaṃ dadyāt svayam utthāpya rāghavaḥ vyavasthāpya mahārājaṃ tvam imaṃ vṛṇuyā varam
english: "When Rāghava himself rises to grant you a boon, having settled the great king, then ask for this boon."

sanskrit: rāmaṃ pravrājayāraṇye nava varṣāṇi pañca ca bharataḥ kriyatāṃ rājā pṛthivyāṃ pārthivarṣabhaḥ
english: "Send Rāma to wander in the forest for fourteen years; let Bharata be made king over the earth — that bull among kings."

sanskrit: evaṃ pravrājitaś caiva rāmo 'rāmo bhaviṣyati bharataś ca hatāmitras tava rājā bhaviṣyati
english: "Thus banished, Rāma will be without Rāma's estate, and Bharata, with his enemies destroyed, will become king for you."

sanskrit: yena kālena rāmaś ca vanāt pratyāgamiṣyati tena kālena putras te kṛtamūlo bhaviṣyati saṃgṛhītamanuṣyaś ca suhṛdbhiḥ sārdham ātmavān
english: "By the time Rāma returns from the forest, your son will have taken root and will have gathered his men, standing firm with his allies, self-possessed."

sanskrit: prāptakālaṃ tu te manye rājānaṃ vītasādhvasā rāmābhiṣekasaṃkalpān nigṛhya vinivartaya
english: "I consider this the right moment — without hesitation, hold back the king and turn him from his resolve to consecrate Rāma."

sanskrit: anartham artharūpeṇa grāhitā sā tatas tayā hṛṣṭā pratītā kaikeyī mantharām idam abravīt
english: Made to embrace disaster in the form of benefit by her, Kaikeyī — now elated and convinced — said this to Mantharā:

sanskrit: kubje tvāṃ nābhijānāmi śreṣṭhāṃ śreṣṭhābhidhāyinīm pṛthivyām asi kubjānām uttamā buddhiniścaye
english: "Hunchback, I did not know you — the best of those who speak of the best! Among all hunchbacks on earth you are the greatest in the resolution of intelligence."

sanskrit: tvam eva tu mamārtheṣu nityayuktā hitaiṣiṇī nāhaṃ samavabudhyeyaṃ kubje rājñaś cikīrṣitam
english: "You alone are ever engaged in my interests and wish me well. I would not have understood what the king intends, O hunchback."

sanskrit: santi duḥsaṃsthitāḥ kubjā vakrāḥ paramapāpikāḥ tvaṃ padmam iva vātena saṃnatā priyadarśanā
english: "There are hunchbacks ill-formed, crooked, supremely wicked — but you, bent by the wind like a lotus, are pleasing to behold."

sanskrit: uras te 'bhiniviṣṭaṃ vai yāvat skandhāt samunnatam adhastāc codaraṃ śāntaṃ sunābham iva lajjitam
english: "Your chest curves inward, rising up to your shoulders, while your belly below is quiet, as though ashamed of its own navel."

sanskrit: jaghanaṃ tava nirghuṣṭaṃ raśanādāmaśobhitam jaṅghe bhṛśam upanyaste pādau cāpy āyatāv ubhau
english: "Your hips are well-formed, adorned with the girdle's cord; your calves are well-placed, and both your feet are long."

sanskrit: tvam āyatābhyāṃ sakthibhyāṃ manthare kṣaumavāsini agrato mama gacchantī rājahaṃsīva rājase
english: "You, Mantharā, clad in silk, going before me on your long thighs, shine like a regal swan."

sanskrit: tavedaṃ sthagu yad dīrghaṃ rathaghoṇam ivāyatam matayaḥ kṣatravidyāś ca māyāś cātra vasanti te
english: "That hump of yours, which is long and extends like the front of a chariot — in it dwell your counsels, your knowledge of statecraft, and your stratagems."

sanskrit: atra te pratimokṣyāmi mālāṃ kubje hiraṇmayīm abhiṣikte ca bharate rāghave ca vanaṃ gate
english: "On it I will fasten a golden garland for you, hunchback, when Bharata has been consecrated and Rāghava has gone to the forest."

sanskrit: jātyena ca suvarṇena suniṣṭaptena sundari labdhārthā ca pratītā ca lepayiṣyāmi te sthagu
english: "With genuine gold, well-refined, O beautiful one — when your purpose is achieved and you are content — I will anoint your hump."

sanskrit: mukhe ca tilakaṃ citraṃ jātarūpamayaṃ śubham kārayiṣyāmi te kubje śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: "I will have a bright auspicious tilaka mark made of gold applied to your face, and fair ornaments adorned on you, hunchback."

sanskrit: paridhāya śubhe vastre devadeva cariṣyasi candram āhvayamānena mukhenāpratimānanā gamiṣyasi gatiṃ mukhyāṃ garvayantī dviṣajjanam
english: "Clad in beautiful garments you will move about like a deity among deities; with a face that rivals the moon, unmatched in beauty, you will go your way as chief among all, making your enemies proud."

sanskrit: tavāpi kubjāḥ kubjāyāḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ pādau paricariṣyanti yathaiva tvaṃ sadā mama
english: "Even other hunchbacks, adorned with all ornaments, will attend upon your feet as you always attend upon mine."

sanskrit: iti praśasyamānā sā kaikeyīm idam abravīt śayānāṃ śayane śubhre vedyām agniśikhām iva
english: Thus praised, she — Mantharā — said this to Kaikeyī as she lay upon her bright couch, like a flame of fire upon an altar:

sanskrit: gatodake setubandho na kalyāṇi vidhīyate uttiṣṭha kuru kalyāṇaṃ rājānam anudarśaya
english: "A dam is not built, dear one, after the waters have gone. Arise, do what is auspicious — show yourself to the king."

sanskrit: tathā protsāhitā devī gatvā mantharayā saha krodhāgāraṃ viśālākṣī saubhāgyamadagarvitā
english: Thus encouraged, the queen — large-eyed, proud in the intoxication of her good fortune — went together with Mantharā and entered the chamber of wrath.

sanskrit: anekaśatasāhasraṃ muktāhāraṃ varāṅganā avamucya varārhāṇi śubhāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: The beautiful woman removed her pearl garland worth many hundreds of thousands, and also her fine and worthy ornaments.

sanskrit: tato hemopamā tatra kubjā vākyaṃ vaśaṃ gatā saṃviśya bhūmau kaikeyī mantharām idam abravīt
english: Then Kaikeyī, golden in complexion, brought under the spell of the hunchback's words, lay down upon the ground there and said this to Mantharā:

sanskrit: iha vā māṃ mṛtāṃ kubje nṛpāyāvedayiṣyasi vanaṃ tu rāghave prāpte bharataḥ prāpsyati kṣitim
english: "Either, hunchback, you will report me dead here — or, when Rāghava has gone to the forest, Bharata will obtain the earth."

sanskrit: athaitad uktvā vacanaṃ sudāruṇaṃ nidhāya sarvābharaṇāni bhāminī asaṃvṛtām āstaraṇena medinīṃ tadādhiśiśye patiteva kinnarī
english: Having spoken those most terrible words, the passionate woman laid aside all her ornaments and lay down upon the bare earth without a covering, like a fallen kinnarī.

sanskrit: udīrṇasaṃrambhatamovṛtānanā tathāvamuktottamamālyabhūṣaṇā narendrapatnī vimanā babhūva sā tamovṛtā dyaur iva magnatārakā
english: Her face veiled in the darkness of surging rage, her finest garlands and ornaments thus cast off, the wife of the lord of men became despondent — like the sky obscured by darkness, its stars submerged.
